close_reason: Added #[non_exhaustive] to pub struct CtLogList. Error enum already had it (the issue's diff was accurate to a stale snapshot — verified live). pkix-ct still builds.
description:
Peer stub crates pkix-ac (lines 41/52/60/70), pkix-revocation-http (line 52), pkix-composite all mark every public enum #[non_exhaustive]. pkix-ct/src/lib.rs:55-66 does NOT, even though it is at version 0.0.0 and is explicitly stub-status:

  #[derive(Debug)]
  // missing #[non_exhaustive]
  pub enum Error {
      NoScts,
      NoTrustedSct,
      InvalidSignature,
      ParseError,
  }

When the crate gains real variants for SCT log-list parsing, RFC 9162 v2 differences, etc., downstream pattern-matches will break.

Fix: add `#[non_exhaustive]` to `pub enum Error` (and to `pub struct CtLogList` at line 41 for the same reason).

Severity: P3 / opinion. The crate is v0.0.0 (deliberately pre-release) so technically there is no compatibility commitment yet, but using #[non_exhaustive] now costs nothing and is consistent with the rest of the workspace. The P4 commit 01908663 already added #[non_exhaustive] to pkix-ac IssuerSerial (PKIX-bcf0); this is the same pattern not applied to pkix-ct.

Pass-1 attribution: pass 1 missed pkix-ct entirely on the non_exhaustive sweep.
title: P3: pkix-ct::Error missing #[non_exhaustive] (inconsistent with peer stub crates)
